findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so the regression test can pass while the NPE happens
findings.body: `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` starts a background thread that repeatedly lists groups and records exceptions into `caughtExceptions`, but the main thread only sets `deletedAll = true` and immediately runs `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())`. There is no `Thread.join()` (and no synchronization between setting the flag and the assertion), so an exception thrown by the very iteration that races with the last deletions – exactly the window this test is meant to cover – can be appended after the assertion has already run, making the test green even when the regression is present. In addition the thread is non-daemon and keeps issuing admin requests after the test method returns (until it observes the flag), which can produce errors/log noise or interfere with teardown of the managed realm and admin client. The thread reference should be kept and joined before asserting.

findings.title: Same concurrent-removal NPE still present in the getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: The fix only guards `getSubGroupsCount()` against `modelSupplier.get()` returning `null`. The three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads (lines 256, 262 and 268) call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` with no null check, and `modelSupplier` resolves to `cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(realm, cached.getId())`, which returns `null` for a group removed by a concurrent transaction after the cache entry was obtained. Under the same race that motivated this PR (listing groups while groups are being deleted) those paths will still throw a NullPointerException, so the reported bug is only partially fixed for group tree/search endpoints.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() now returns null, which is not part of the GroupModel contract
findings.body: `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` returns `null` when the underlying group no longer exists. `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` returns a boxed `Long` but no implementation (e.g. the JPA adapter) ever returns `null` and the interface documents no nullability, so callers are free to unbox or compare the result. Any such caller now gets a NullPointerException at the call site instead of here – i.e. the NPE is relocated rather than removed – and REST responses can silently carry `subGroupCount: null`. Prefer returning `0L` (or handling the removed-group case explicitly, e.g. by skipping the group) instead of leaking `null` through the model API.

findings.title: populateGroupHierarchyFromSubGroups still dereferences a possibly-removed parent group
findings.body: In `populateGroupHierarchyFromSubGroups`, `session.groups().getGroupById(realm, currGroup.getParentId())` can return `null` when the parent group is deleted concurrently with the listing request. `parentModel` is then passed to `groupEvaluator.canView(parentModel)` (line 51), to `toRepresentation(groupEvaluator, parentModel, full)` (line 57) and to `populateSubGroupCount(parentModel, parent)` (line 60) without any null check, producing a NullPointerException on exactly the concurrent read/delete path this PR aims to fix (and unconditionally when fine-grained admin permissions are enabled, since the `canView` block is skipped). A null `parentModel` should abort the walk for that branch (e.g. remove the current group from the map and break), analogous to the existing not-viewable handling.

findings.title: Shared admin client used from two threads may yield spurious failures
findings.body: The background reader calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` while the main thread performs deletes through the same injected `Keycloak` admin client. The admin client's token manager/JAX-RS proxy is not documented as thread-safe; concurrent token refresh from two threads can produce intermittent 401/`NotAuthorizedException`, which this test would record in `caughtExceptions` and report as a failure of the group-listing code. Using a separate admin client instance (or at least a dedicated token) for the reader thread would avoid attributing client-side races to the server fix being tested.

findings.title: Tight busy loop issuing unbounded group queries
findings.body: The reader thread loops with no pause, each iteration requesting `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)`. This saturates a CPU and floods the server with full-table group listings for the whole duration of the 100 deletions, slowing the test suite and making timing-sensitive neighbouring tests more flaky. A small sleep between iterations (and a bounded `maxResults`) would keep the race window without the load.

findings.title: Created groups are not registered for cleanup
findings.body: The 100 groups created in `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` are only removed by the explicit delete loop; nothing is registered with `managedRealm.cleanup()`. If any `remove()` call or an earlier assertion fails, the remaining `Test Group N` entries stay in the realm, which is shared by all other test methods in this class, so a single failure here can cascade into unrelated failures in group-listing tests.
